title: Display and Normal Flow
description: Understand the browser's default document layout engine: master block vs inline formatting contexts, inline-block hybrid behavior, and display: none visibility mechanics.

objectives.statement: Differentiate formatting rules across block, inline, and inline-block display values.
Control element layout and document flow using display: none versus visibility: hidden.

content.title: The Browser's Normal Flow Engine
content.hook: Before Flexbox or Grid ever existed, browsers arranged documents using Normal Flow. Understanding block and inline behavior is essential to controlling document geometry.
content.context:
`block` elements (like `
`, `

`) stack vertically and take 100% parent width. `inline` elements (like ``, ``) flow side-by-side with text and ignore explicit `width` and `height`. `inline-block` provides the best of both worlds.
goals: Understand how block and inline elements participate in Normal Flow.
Apply `display: inline-block` to give inline elements dimensions and vertical padding.
Distinguish `display: none` (removes from flow) from `visibility: hidden` (reserves space).

content.title: Block vs Inline vs Inline-Block
content.description: Block: Stacks vertically, fills 100% width, respects all box properties. Inline: Sits in text line, ignores width/height/vertical margins. Inline-block: Sits in text line side-by-side, but respects width, height, and all padding/margins.

content.prompt: A developer writes `span.tag { width: 120px; height: 40px; margin-top: 20px; }` without changing the display property. What happens to the rendered `<span>`?
content.code: Order status: Pending
options: The span expands to 120px by 40px and pushes the paragraph down by 20px
The span ignores width, height, and margin-top because inline elements cannot have dimensional box constraints in normal flow
The span converts automatically into a block element
The browser throws a CSS parsing exception

validation.expected: The span ignores width, height, and margin-top because inline elements cannot have dimensional box constraints in normal flow

feedback.correct: Spot on! Default `inline` elements flow with text lines and completely ignore `width`, `height`, `margin-top`, and `margin-bottom`. To respect dimensions, change display to `inline-block` or `block`.
feedback.incorrect: By default, `<span>` is an inline element. Inline elements ignore explicit width, height, and vertical margins in normal flow.

content.title: Build Inline-Block Navigation Buttons
content.prompt:
Style the navigation links `.nav-btn` and notice how changing `display` affects layout:
1. Set `display: inline-block` on `.nav-btn` so they sit side-by-side while respecting box dimensions.
2. Add `padding: 8px 16px`, `background-color: #2563eb`, `color: #ffffff`, and `text-decoration: none`.
3. Add `margin-right: 12px` to separate the buttons.
4. Set `display: none` on `.hidden-item` to remove it from the page.
content.starterCode: Dashboard Settings Admin Only

testCases.description: .nav-btn must have blue background #2563eb / rgb(37, 99, 235) and white text

feedback.correct: Terrific! `inline-block` allowed the anchor links to sit on the same line while accepting padding, margins, and dimension controls.
feedback.incorrect: Review your rules: set `display: inline-block; padding: 8px 16px; background-color: #2563eb; color: #ffffff; text-decoration: none; margin-right: 12px;` on `.nav-btn`, and `display: none;` on `.hidden-item`.

hints.content: Add `.nav-btn { display: inline-block; padding: 8px 16px; background-color: #2563eb; color: #ffffff; text-decoration: none; margin-right: 12px; }`.
Add `.hidden-item { display: none; }` to completely remove the item from the rendered flow.

content.prompt: What is the critical behavioral difference between `display: none` and `visibility: hidden` regarding layout space and screen readers?

feedback.correct: Great analysis! `display: none` removes the element entirely from the layout flow and accessibility tree (taking 0 space), whereas `visibility: hidden` makes the element invisible but preserves its exact box dimensions in the layout.
feedback.incorrect: Think about whether empty space remains on the screen and whether the element participates in layout calculation.

content.title: Key Takeaways: Display & Normal Flow
takeaways: Block elements start on a new line and expand to fill available parent width.
Inline elements flow within line boxes and ignore explicit width, height, and vertical margins.
Inline-block elements flow horizontally while accepting full box model dimensions and padding.
display: none removes elements from the document flow and accessibility tree entirely.
visibility: hidden hides elements visually while preserving their physical layout space.
